legislation.notes: Approved by the Governor and filed with the Secretary of State on 30 September 2026; Chapter 985, Statutes of 2026. Title: "Electricity: portable solar generation devices." The act states no operative date. Under the California Constitution, Art. IV §8(c)(1), a statute goes into effect on January 1 next following a 90-day period from enactment, so SB 868 takes effect on 1 January 2027; that date comes from the Constitution, not from the text of the act. Pub. Util. Code §8530(c): a portable solar generation device has a maximum aggregated AC output of no more than 1,200 watts per dwelling, is designed to connect through a receptacle, meets the National Electrical Code and the California Electrical Code, is certified as a plug-in photovoltaic system by Underwriters Laboratories or an equivalent nationally recognized testing laboratory, and includes a certified feature that prevents backfeeding during an outage. §8531 exempts it from all interconnection requirements; a utility may require a simple online registration of address, make, model and size, which "shall not require approval", and may not charge a fee or require additional controls. §8531(e): "This section shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2030, and as of that date is repealed." §8532: beginning 1 January 2030, a receptacle-connected portable photovoltaic device that does not meet §8530(c)(4) to (6) shall not be sold or offered for sale in the state. Earlier history: introduced 5 January 2026; passed the Senate 35-1 on 21 April 2026; enrolled 28 August and presented to the Governor 31 August 2026. The record names no signatory. Read from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov (bill status and chaptered text) on 7 October 2026.

certification_requirement.quote: Is certified as a plug-in photovoltaic system by Underwriters Laboratories, or an equivalent nationally recognized testing laboratory.
certification_requirement.note: Verbatim from the primary text, paragraph (5). Paragraph (6) separately requires a feature, certified by Underwriters Laboratories or an equivalent nationally recognized testing laboratory, that prevents backfeeding during an outage. The effective date comes from the California Constitution, Art. IV §8(c)(1), not from the act. 'Nationally recognized testing laboratory' is the term used in 29 C.F.R. 1910.7; UL, CSA and Intertek/ETL are all NRTLs. A CE mark is a European self-declaration and is not an NRTL listing.
